andr36oid turns this console into an Android handheld. Games, emulators and apps, all run with the buttons, no touchscreen needed.

Forgot one? Hold FN on its own for a moment, in any app or game, and this list shows up. Let go of FN to close it.
Your games
Games go on the EASYROMS partition of the SD card. In a computer, the card shows up as a drive called EASYROMS. On the console, it\'s the EASYROMS storage in the Files app.
Give every system its own folder, named like nes, snes, gb, gba, megadrive or psx. Cards set up for ArkOS or dArkOS already use these names, so their games work as they are.
The console makes these folders on EASYROMS by itself, with a README listing which system goes where.

No computer or card reader at hand? Open Wi-Fi transfer on the console and scan its QR code with your phone, or type the address it shows into any browser on the same network, to send games straight to EASYROMS.
Daijishou, the home screen, turns those folders into a game library: add a platform and pick its folder on EASYROMS.

Daijishou, the home screen, already has a platform for each of these systems, set to its folder on EASYROMS. The first time it opens, it asks to look for games: press OK. When you add games later, it asks again at the next start. Games added while the console is on show up after Sync entirely in Daijishou\'s library settings. For other systems, or on a card set up with .noroms, add a platform in Daijishou and pick its folder.

Your home screen is Simple UI, which shows apps, not games. For a game library, open Daijishou from Apps: it already knows these folders and asks to look for games when you open it. Or start a game straight from RetroArch with Load Content, or from PPSSPP\'s game list.

Your home screen is Simple UI, which shows apps, not games. Start a game from RetroArch with Load Content, or from PPSSPP\'s game list, and pick it in its folder on EASYROMS. To get Daijishou\'s game library back, go to Settings > Apps & notifications > Home screen.
Emulators

RetroArch and PPSSPP come preinstalled, with Flycast (Dreamcast), Mupen64Plus AE (N64) and EasyRPG Player. RetroArch already has cores for Nintendo, Sega, PlayStation, N64, arcade, Neo Geo, PC Engine, Atari, MSX, DOS, Amiga, ZX Spectrum, C64, PICO-8 and more. The README on EASYROMS lists which folder goes with which system.
PSP games run in PPSSPP. PlayStation games start without a BIOS, but work best with one in the bios folder on EASYROMS.
The emulators are ordinary apps: you can uninstall them, and if you install F-Droid, it can update them.
Playing with a second controller

Plug a USB pad into the OTG port, with an adapter if needed. For a Bluetooth pad, open Settings > Controls > External controllers > Pair a Bluetooth controller, put the pad into pairing mode and press A on it in the list. The page says how pairing mode works on Xbox, PlayStation, Switch and 8BitDo pads.
In RetroArch the console\'s own buttons stay player 1. Extra pads are player 2, 3 and so on, in the order you first press a button on them.
Want to play alone on the bigger pad? Set Settings > Controls > Player 1 in RetroArch to External controller. Quit RetroArch first; the change counts from its next start.

On any pad, L1 + R1 + Start + Select, or the Xbox, PS or Capture button, opens the RetroArch menu. Start + Select pressed twice quits the game. PSP games have only one player, and every pad controls it.
Speed and battery

Settings > Performance has three profiles. Battery saver for long sessions with older systems, Balanced for everyday use, Performance for PS1, N64 and PSP. The Quick Settings tile switches between them too.
Settings > CPU overclock (experimental) runs the processor faster than standard for demanding games. A restart turns it off. If the console freezes, pick a lower speed.
CPU overclock (experimental), on the same page, runs the processor faster than standard for demanding games. A restart turns it off. If the console freezes, pick a lower speed.

Short on memory? Switch on Close background apps when opening any game in Settings > Performance. It closes your other apps when a game starts and tells you how many. The power menu has Close background apps too.

The power menu shows how the console is doing along the top: CPU, TEMP, BAT, RAM and SD. SD is how busy the card is in %, with its read and write speed: a green up arrow while it mostly reads, a red down arrow while it mostly writes.
In the Performance overlay, with SD card activity ticked, STOR is how busy the SD card is in %. It is not how full the card is.
The screen uses the most power. Lower brightness means longer play time.
Mouse and buttons
Hold both sticks pressed in for a second: joystick mouse on or off
Move the pointer
Click, hold R1 to drag
Right click
Scroll
Settings > Controls > Joystick mouse changes speed, buttons and the combination.
Settings > Controls > Button mapping swaps buttons, with profiles for different games.
Locked yourself out? Hold both volume buttons for 5 seconds and every button is back to normal.
Touch controls

Some games only work with a touchscreen. Touch controls give such a game its own layout: each button or stick touches a spot on the screen. It switches on by itself while that game is in front; every other app keeps the normal buttons.
In the game: open the editor on top of it
Or go to Settings > Controls > Touch controls > Add an app. The game starts and the editor opens on top.
Move the crosshair to a spot
Add a control there, then press its button or move its stick
Make the selected control smaller or bigger
Save and go back to the game
A control can tap, hold, swipe, work as an on-screen joystick, or look around like a camera. Select in the editor has more: a shift button for a second set of controls, and the on-screen labels.
Buttons without a control still work as normal buttons, and FN with its shortcuts always works.
Going online

Most R36S consoles have no Wi-Fi built in, but some models, such as the R36XX, do. If yours has it, just turn on Wi-Fi in Settings > Wi-Fi & Bluetooth. If not, plug a USB Wi-Fi adapter into the OTG port, with a USB-C adapter if it needs one, then turn on Wi-Fi there. Bluetooth devices are on the same page, under Bluetooth & devices.
Thorium is the web browser.
Troubleshooting
Most problems can be fixed with a computer and the SD card. On a computer, the card shows a small drive called BOOT (the start files) and a big one called EASYROMS (your games).
The first start takes a long time

That\'s normal. The first start sets up the SD card and restarts on its own, then Android prepares its apps. A setup screen shows the steps, a progress bar and the time left, and the home screen opens when it\'s done. Give it a few minutes, up to 10 on a slow card, and don\'t switch it off.
The screen stays black on the first start, but the console is on

Your console has a different screen than the one this card was set up for. On a computer, open BOOT, then Panels. Copy all files from one of the Panel folders to the top of BOOT and replace the files there. Panel4 is the default, so try the others one at a time.
It stopped starting after an update or a Magisk module

Start it without root. On a computer, open BOOT and rename ramdisk.uimg to ramdisk-magisk.uimg, then rename ramdisk-stock.uimg to ramdisk.uimg. Your apps and games stay. Rename them back later to get root again.
The console froze
Hold Power for about 10 seconds until it switches off, then switch it on again. If it froze with the CPU overclock on, pick a lower speed next time. A restart always turns the overclock off.
A game doesn\'t start, or starts to a black screen

Some systems, like Sega CD and PC Engine CD, need a file from the original console (a BIOS), and PlayStation games work better with one. Put these files in the bios folder on EASYROMS. Settings > Emulator files shows what\'s missing.
The buttons do the wrong thing
Sticks drift or don\'t reach the edge

Open Settings > Controls > Calibrate sticks and press A. Move both sticks in full circles, slowly and all the way to the edge. Then let go of them and press A. From then on every game and app uses the corrected sticks, also after a restart.
Still creeping a little? Left and right on the D-pad change the dead zone, the part around the middle that is ignored. Press X twice to go back to the factory settings.
Recovery and factory reset
Hold FN while you switch the console on

This starts the recovery menu. If holding FN does nothing (Soy Sauce and some other clones), put an empty file named recovery.txt on BOOT with a computer instead, and delete it again afterwards: as long as it is there, every start goes into recovery. In the recovery menu, move with the d-pad or the volume buttons, choose with A or Power. For a factory reset, pick Factory reset, then Format data/factory reset, then Reboot system now. This erases your apps, your settings and all files in internal storage, but not the games on EASYROMS. Don\'t use the other options: this recovery is older than your system and can\'t install updates for it.
The date or time is wrong
The console forgets the time when the battery runs completely empty. Set it in Settings > System > Date & time. With a network connection it sets itself, as long as "Use network-provided time" is on.
If your console won\'t start
Try these steps in order. None of them touches your games on EASYROMS.
Safe mode
Hold Vol− while you switch the console on, until the home screen shows

Switch it off first; hold Power for 10 seconds if it hangs. In safe mode, "Safe mode" shows in the bottom left corner and apps you installed yourself don\'t run, RetroArch and PPSSPP too. Uninstall the app that causes trouble, or change the setting back. Restart normally to leave safe mode.
It stopped starting after a Magisk module

Switch it off and on again, up to three times. After two starts that don\'t finish, Magisk turns all modules off by itself. Safe mode turns them off too. They stay off until you turn them back on, one by one, in the Magisk app.
USB and computers
The easiest way to copy games is to put the SD card into a computer and copy them to EASYROMS. Put the card back before you switch the console on.
Connect the console to a computer

Turn on Settings > USB mode > Connect to a computer, then plug a data cable into the OTG port and a USB-A port on the computer. File transfer is on by default; Use USB for, on the same page, switches to photo transfer or adb only. Pads and adapters on the OTG port don\'t work while this is on, and a restart turns it off.

Never turn this on if your console has Wi-Fi built in, such as the R36XX. Those consoles use this same USB port for their Wi-Fi, so Wi-Fi stops working and may not come back until you restart. USB mode asks before it switches.
Never use this while the console is charging from its other port. Unplug the charger first. If a charger is plugged in while it is on, USB mode switches back to accessories.
For adb, also turn on USB debugging in Settings > System > Developer options. To show Developer options, press A on Build number 7 times in Settings > About console.
The OTG port is for accessories: pads, USB drives and network adapters. It can\'t connect to a computer on this build.
Accessories

Plug accessories into the OTG port, with a USB-C adapter or a small hub if needed. USB pads, keyboards, mice, USB drives, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and Ethernet adapters work if Android has a driver for their chip. Adapters with common Realtek chips work best. On consoles with Wi-Fi built in, such as the R36XX, something plugged into the OTG port can stop the built-in Wi-Fi.
Nothing happens? Unplug it, wait a few seconds and plug it in again. Some adapters need more power than the port gives; a hub with its own power supply helps.
SD card

The card holds everything: Android, your apps and data (half the card, between 16 and 64 GB), and EASYROMS, which gets the rest. On a card of 16 GB or less, Android takes the whole card and there is no EASYROMS. EASYROMS uses exFAT, so Windows, macOS and Linux can all read it.
All the space for apps, no EASYROMS

Before the very first start, make an empty file named .noroms on BOOT. The first start then gives the whole card to apps. Or, to pick the size, write a number of GB (or all) into a file named userdata-size.txt on BOOT. This only works on a freshly written card. BIOS files then go in the bios folder on the internal storage.
Back up your saves

Saves made next to the games on EASYROMS are easy to copy on a computer. Saves inside an app stay with that app on the Android part of the card, so check each emulator\'s settings for where it keeps them.
Keep your saves the same on two devices

Settings > Save backup > Sync saves keeps your save games and save states the same on this console and your PC, phone or another console, over your home Wi-Fi. There is no cloud and no account, and games and BIOS files are never copied. It syncs while the console charges on Wi-Fi, and while that page is open.

On a PC or phone, install Syncthing and add the console\'s ID from that page, or scan its code. The PC or phone then shows up on the console under Add a device: press A on it. For two consoles, turn on Sync saves on both, then pick each one on the other. Quit the game before you play on the other device.
Battery care
The battery percentage looks wrong

The battery gauge guesses the charge and learns as it goes. After the battery ran empty or the console sat unused for a long time, charge it to 100% with the console on and leave it on the charger for another half hour. That lets the gauge find the right level again. If you set a charge limit in Settings > Battery > Battery details, turn it off for this.
Settings > Battery > Battery details shows the battery voltage: about 4.2 V is full, below 3.5 V is nearly empty.
Sleep or power off?
Sleep (tap Power) is fine for breaks, but still uses a little battery. For more than a day, power it off from the power menu.
Putting it away for a while
Charge it to about half and power it off. Top it up every few months. A battery left completely empty for a long time can wear out.
Using a clone console
Many consoles look like the R36S but are built differently inside. The card starts with the files for the genuine R36S. A clone usually needs other files from the BOOT drive of the SD card.
Which folder

On a computer, open BOOT. Panels has a folder for each genuine R36S screen and the R36S Plus. Experimental has a folder for each known clone, such as K36, G80, R36 Max, R36 Ultra and the Soy Sauce boards. The README.txt in Panels and in Experimental says which console goes with which folder. The Experimental files are untested, so only use them if Panels doesn\'t work.
Soy Sauce boards (Y3506 printed on the board) must never use Panel5 or Panel6, even if the screen looks right. Use a Soy folder in Experimental.
Copy all files

First make a folder called Backup on BOOT and copy these files from the top of BOOT into it: rk3326-r36s-android.dtb, the six rg351 files, logo.bmp, logo_kernel.bmp and the battery_*.bmp files. Then copy all files from your folder to the top of BOOT and replace the ones there. Really all of them: the six rg351 files are the same file under six names, and your console picks the one it wants.
The screen stays black, or the buttons don\'t work

Try the next folder that could fit your console. If only the boot logo stays black but Android comes up, keep it. To go back, copy the files from your Backup folder, or from Panels/Panel4, to the top of BOOT.
Some clones, like the R36 Ultra, R36 Max and R39 Max, start from their own built-in memory first and may not look at the SD card at all.

Root (Magisk)
The console comes with root through Magisk, but it is off until you set it up once.
Turn root on: open Magisk once first
Open the Magisk app and let it finish its setup. It asks to restart the console: say yes. Only after that restart do you have root.
From then on, apps that ask for root show a prompt: allow or deny it with the buttons. The Magisk app manages root access and modules.
Root lives on the BOOT part of the card, so it stays when the system is updated.
A module broke the start
See Troubleshooting: on BOOT, swap ramdisk.uimg for ramdisk-stock.uimg, and the console starts without root and modules.
